chapter: Williams on guitarists, family and touring
title: A woman guitarist who outplayed Henry Gaines
summary: Williams tells of a woman guitarist who played with a bar on her finger and beat Henry Gaines, who then wanted to attack her.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: So, and, uh, this lady, uh, they called her, uh, she, she wore her hair just like a man with a brace back, you know. Texas. They called it Texas. They had a play with Annie Allison one night and that woman could do more with a guitar and a monkey could with a coconut. She could. That woman could play in there. And so, she was there for the play that night. Henry Gaines walked in and he asked her, let me play with you. She told him, come out. She played with a bar neck on her finger just like Freddie McDowell do. Mm-hmm.
Well, that woman taking that guitar there.
Oh, my God. I don't believe a monkey could wrestle with a coconut as good as she could play that guitar. So, Henry Gaines, he got mad cause she beat him playing a guitar. Yeah, yeah.
And, and, and want to jump on her.
Yeah. People's up there got, uh, scared of him because he, uh, he packs a little gun, you see.
What's up, you guys, Barney? I didn't, I didn't, I didn't hear you. What about? Okay. I see you all later.
